name: Carrow Dockside Denim Jacket
description:
A heavy-weight raw denim jacket in indigo-black, cut boxy and generous through the shoulders with reinforced elbows and a double-button chest. The fabric is stiff when new and softens into creases unique to each wearer over months of use. Contrast stitching in burnt orange runs along the seams. Four exterior pockets, all with button closures. The collar is unlined and slightly oversized — good for turning up against lake wind.

Carrow is a Tier 2 street label out of the old Pilsen manufacturing district. No tech, no gimmicks. Workers, students, and anyone who appreciates something that lasts wear this jacket until it falls apart, then wear it a little longer.
what_it_says: You work hard and you don't need to announce it. You've had this jacket for three years and plan to have it for ten more.
worn_by: Shelf climbers who made it to Tier 2
story_hooks: A serial number stamped inside the collar traces back to a Carrow run that was supposedly destroyed — the batch linked to a labor dispute three years ago
The previous owner's name is written in marker on the inner chest pocket, and that person is now missing
A fence at the Pilsen market is offering these at half price, no questions asked — too many of them, all the same size

physical_description.visual_profile: A boxy, broad-shouldered silhouette that reads authoritative and grounded. The jacket has a workwear attitude—intentionally oversized through the chest and arms, with a dropped shoulder seam that sits naturally on varied frame sizes. When worn, it commands presence without trying.
physical_description.fit: Generous and relaxed through the torso, with room for layering underneath. The sleeves are straight and slightly long, ending just below the wrist bone. The length hits at mid-hip. Built for movement, not restriction.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy-weight raw indigo-black denim, selvedge edge construction. Stiff and rigid when new; develops unique creasing and fading patterns with wear. The fabric has visible nubs and irregularities from traditional loom weaving.
physical_description.texture: Crisp and slightly rough to the touch when new, with a subtle nap. Stitching creates raised seams that soften over time. Elbows feature a tighter weave for durability. The collar is raw-edged and unstructured, prone to curling naturally.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep indigo-black base with burnt orange contrast stitching on all seams, pocket edges, and button reinforcement. The indigo fades to lighter blue-gray at stress points with age, creating an organic wear map.
physical_description.closures: Four exterior pockets with individual button closures. Dual-button chest configuration (stacked vertically, spaced 3 inches apart). Metal shank buttons in brushed steel, designed for gloved hands.
distinctive_features: Reinforced elbows with double-layer denim patch
Oversized, unlined collar that turns up easily
Visible selvage edge on pocket openings
Double-button chest unique to Carrow's signature
No logos, no branding patches—bare tag sewn inside
Designed to develop unique creasing and fade patterns
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2–3 boundary. Carrow is accessible working-class wear with quality that justifies the price. Appeals to people who see clothing as investment, not disposal.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by dock workers, fabricators, students, and anyone in the GLMZ who respects durability and simplicity. No augmentation necessary—this jacket works alongside chrome and skin equally. It signals: I work, I plan to be here a while, I don't follow trends.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine and stiff when new (first 3–6 months). Gradually broken-in, with creases forming at elbows and shoulders. After a year, fading appears at pocket corners, cuffs, and seams. Well-worn examples show patina; some wearers patch rips with visible repair stitching rather than retire the jacket.
